DRW Singapore Pte Ltd's audited accounts (Companies House FC036980) show total net revenue of $408.8m for FY2023 and $269.4m for FY2022, so neither year matches. FY2023 total net revenue includes $291.8m of interest income almost exactly offset by $291.9m of finance costs; net of that it is about $117m. The FT's $282mn 'net book value' of linked subsidiaries also sits close to, but not exactly on, the $276.5m 'investment in subsidiaries' at end-2023. Treat the FT's Singapore figures as unreconciled. 2) The FT's unnamed 'London-based subsidiary [that] made almost $1bn in revenue over 2017 and 2018' and then 'stopped filing accounts' could not be identified. DRW Investments (UK) Ltd (02329842) and DRW Global Markets Ltd (09240825, renamed Feb 2020) both filed full accounts every year 2016-2025, so the entity is something else, possibly re-registered as unlimited or converted. The filings lens should check this. 3) Scope of the $176m 2026 figure. eFinancialCareers (citing the FT) says 'the firm made an adjusted loss of $176m in the first quarter of 2026', and the FT headline says 'Group took $176mn hit'. Crypto Briefing and ValueTheMarkets frame it as a power and gas desk loss, and EnkiAI dates it to Feb 2026. It may be a firm-wide adjusted Q1 result or a desk loss, so do not double-count. 4) The Bloomberg 2020 figures come from 'people familiar' during a loan process; the article was not fetched, but its wording is confirmed by several matching snippets. 'Revenue' is undefined and could be gross of trading costs. As a DRW Holdings figure it may include real-estate (Convexity) and VC gains, which are out of scope; Moody's noted real-estate and VC investments as a share of tangible equity. 5) Aggregator revenue estimates range from $65m (PrivCo 2020, likely a broker-dealer or modeled figure) to about $5bn (algotradingmap, undated, in an AUM column), with ZoomInfo at $1bn, Owler at $100-500m, Growjo at $533m and RocketReach at $670m. If held at DRW, crypto mark-to-market could swing reported 'revenue' in 2017, 2020-21 and 2024-25, so exclude it if personal. 10) Revelio headcount data (2,032-2,528) is internally inconsistent and probably includes affiliates and contractors.
evidence.summary:
The press record of DRW's firm-wide PnL is very thin: DRW is private and, as the FT said in Nov 2024, 'its revenue and profit figures are private'. 
- **2020/2019 (only firm-wide annual figure):** Bloomberg (18 Jun 2021, people familiar, during a loan process) reported 2020 revenue up 50% to about $1.5bn and EBITDA up 67% to about $750m. That implies about $1.0bn revenue and about $450m EBITDA for 2019. Moody's (Feb 2021) separately cited strong 2020 earnings. 
- **2026 YTD:** the FT (12 Jun 2026), via eFinancialCareers (4 Aug 2026), reported an adjusted loss of $176m in Q1 2026, tied to power and gas trading during the winter storm, after which the North American gas and power head left (Bloomberg, 16 Jun 2026). It is unclear whether this is a group-wide result or a desk loss; there is nothing after Q1 2026. 
- **Cumberland:** the SEC complaint (10 Oct 2024) alleges more than $400m revenue and more than $27m profit cumulatively from Mar 2018 to Oct 2024. The case was dismissed in Mar 2025. 
- **Partial-entity data:** FT Nov 2024 says a London subsidiary made almost $1bn revenue across 2017-2018 (unnamed), and a Singapore subsidiary made $312mn net revenue 'last year', which does not match the accounts. I pulled and read the audited DRW Singapore Pte Ltd accounts filed at Companies House. Total net revenue ($m): 83.7 (2018), 83.7 (2019), 195.3 (2020), 112.5 (2021), 269.4 (2022), 408.8 (2023, inflated by ~$292m interest pass-through), 252.5 (2024), 149.3 (2025). Profit after tax ($m): 12.9, 1.4, 72.6, 21.8, 63.9, 44.8, 90.2, 14.9. 
- **UK:** DRW UK Partners LLP went from a £6.2m profit (2024) to a £3.5m operating loss (2025). Staff rose from 322 to 376, and average wages and salaries from £321k to £340.9k. 
- **Headcount (press):** more than 500 (Jan 2015, before Chopper's ~200 joined), 700 (Mar 2016), 725 (Dec 2016), about 2,100 (Nov 2024), about 2,000 including 800+ technologists (2025/early 2026). 
- **Per head:** the 2020 figure implies roughly $1.0-1.5m revenue per head, assuming about 1,000-1,500 staff in 2020; no 2020 headcount was found. 
- **Aggregator estimates** ($65m to $5bn) are unreliable and contradictory. 
- **For estimation:** treat 2015-2018 and 2021-2025 as unreported by the press. Anchor 2019-2020 on Bloomberg, use Singapore and UK subsidiary trends for direction only (2020 strong, 2021 weaker, 2022-2023 strong, 2024 solid, 2025 weaker for Singapore), and use the Q1 2026 loss for 2026 YTD.

evidence.red_flags:
1) FT, Nov 2024: '$312mn in net revenues' for a Singapore subsidiary in 2023. This matches DRW Singapore Pte Ltd's original FY2023 'total net revenue' of S$408.8m converted to dollars, but S$291.8m of that was repo interest income offset by S$291.9m of finance costs. The FY2024 accounts restated FY2023 to S$121.2m. The FT also says the unit was 'set up in 2017', but the company was incorporated in 2014 (UEN 201428336M). Do not use $312m as Singapore trading revenue.
2) FT, Nov 2024: 'a single London-based subsidiary made almost $1bn in revenue over 2017 and 2018'. It is actually DRW Investments, LLC, an Illinois LLC that filed whole-entity accounts at Companies House because it had a UK branch. Actual total revenue was $863m ($487m + $376m), and that is gross of about $82-84m a year in trading costs.
3) Bloomberg, June 2021 ($1.5bn revenue / $750m EBITDA): anonymous sources at a time when the firm was raising loans, and the revenue definition (gross vs net of fees) is not stated. I verified it only through search snippets of the syndicated copy; I could not fetch the Bloomberg page.
4) The UK entities' revenues and profits are set by group transfer pricing. DRW Investments (UK) Ltd revenue was GBP 0.3m in 2025 and DRW Global Markets Ltd GBP 26.7m in 2023, and neither has employees. DRW UK Partners LLP turnover (GBP 202m in 2025) is service fees plus performance fees, not trading revenue. eFinancialCareers' 'DRW made a loss in its UK entity' (GBP 3.4m) is a service-entity residual and says nothing about trading performance.
5) Beagle and similar sites present Form 5500 BEGINNING-of-year TOTAL participants (843 to 1,523), which include departed vested employees, as if they were employee counts. Use the active end-of-year counts. The DOL welfare-plan active count for 2023 (1,725) is an outlier against the 401(k) figure (1,174) and the plan's own 2024 figures (1,753 at the start, 1,205 at the end).
6) Aggregator revenue figures are wildly inconsistent: PrivCo $90-250m (2021-23), Owler $100-500m, ZoomInfo $1bn, RocketReach $670m, AlgoTradingMap about $5bn. PrivCo is plainly wrong given primary data. Aggregator headcounts range from 1,039 to 2,553.
7) Cumberland: the SEC's 'more than $400m revenue / $27m profit' is cumulative from March 2018 to October 2024, covers one legal entity, and is an allegation in a case dismissed in March 2025. Do not annualise it as Cumberland's economic PnL; some crypto trading may sit in other entities (Cumberland SG, affiliates).
8) The $176m loss: eFinancialCareers frames it as an 'adjusted loss in Q1 2026'; other outlets tie it to the January 2026 winter storm. It is a single desk, not the firm. Moody's put DRW on review for downgrade on 2026-06-16, citing a trading-risk appetite 'higher than peers' and earnings volatility.
9) Scope contamination: S&P says commercial real estate and venture capital make up 5-10% of DRW's net revenue. Any firm-wide revenue figure (including Bloomberg's) probably includes them and should be reduced by about 5-10%.
10) DRW Singapore's figures are company-only in SGD and include upstream dividends from its Dutch subsidiaries (S$92.9m in 2024), so they double-count group trading if added to DRW Europe.
evidence.summary:
Primary-document findings for DRW, 2015-2026:
(a) Bloomberg (June 2021) is the only firm-wide PnL figure: 2020 revenue about $1.5bn (+50%) and EBITDA about $750m (+67%). That implies about $1.0bn and $450m for 2019.
(b) Audited US-GAAP accounts of DRW Investments, LLC, DRW's main US prop-trading subsidiary, filed at UK Companies House because of its UK branch, cover 2014-2018. Total revenue was $357m, $470m, $455m, $487m and $376m. Net of trading costs (my derivation) it was $307m, $411m, $379m, $405m and $292m. Net income was $199m, $272m, $246m, $270m and $131m, with compensation of $62-91m. This is a hard floor for firm-wide PnL in those years. It also explains the FT's 'almost $1bn' figure for 2017-18 (actually $863m).
(c) DRW Singapore Pte Ltd's accounts (SGD, company-only, filed at Companies House) cover 2017-2025. Total net revenue was S$40m, 84m, 84m, 195m, 113m, 269m (grossed up), 121m (restated 2023), 253m (including a S$93m subsidiary dividend) and 149m. Profit before tax was S$1.6m, 15.9m, 1.6m, 84m, 24.8m, 70m, 48m, 91m and 21m. The FT's '$312mn' for 2023 is a grossed-up figure, later restated.
(d) Rating agencies (Moody's and S&P release texts, via the Troubled Company Reporter) are qualitative only: strong 2020 and 2021; solid 2023 and 2024 'to date'; 2024 'good but not as strong' as peers, with 'lower-than-peer profitability'. Commercial real estate and venture capital are 5-10% of net revenue. Term-loan debt grew from $300m (2019) to $500m (2021), $900m (2024) and $1.15bn (Dec 2024). Moody's placed DRW on review for downgrade on 2026-06-16, after a reported $176m Q1 2026 loss on the North American power/gas desk.
(e) Headcount: Moody's said over 1,000 employees in ten offices (Nov 2019); the FT said about 2,100 (Nov 2024); the website says over 2,000 (2026). US 401(k) active participants at year-end, from the DOL Form 5500 data I downloaded, were 394, 497, 500, 580, 614, 688, 746, 826, 967, 1,174 and 1,262 for 2014-2024. UK LLP average staff were 37, 32, 38, 58, 65, 63, 94, 169, 291, 322 and 376 for FY2014/15 through FY2025. The 401(k) count is roughly 60-69% of the firm-wide total.
Overall: PnL is only well anchored for 2020 (about $1.3-1.5bn net trading revenue after stripping roughly 5-10% CRE/VC income). Other years need peer and ratio estimates with wide error bars, using the DRW Investments, LLC floor for 2015-2018 and the qualitative rating commentary for 2021-2025.

evidence.gaps:
1) No primary firm-wide headcount exists for any year. DRW is private, files no 10-K, and has no Form ADV with employee counts. Firm-wide figures are press descriptors: >500 (Jan 2015, pre-Chopper), 700 (Mar 2016), 725 (Dec 2016), ~900 (Oct 2018), ~1,700 (Jul 2023), and 'over 2,000' (FIA Mar 2025, Wikipedia/FN 2025, drw.com Oct 2026).
2) There is no dated firm-wide figure for 2019, 2020, 2021 or 2022. Those years can only be built bottom-up: US 401(k) active participants (688 / 746 / 826 / 967) plus UK LLP (65 / 63 / 94 / 169) plus Singapore (~40-55) plus Canada (unknown before 2026, ~300 by 2025-26) plus small offices.
3) Canada (Montreal) headcount is missing for 2015-2024. The 298 FT figure is from the Mar 2026 profile only, and the gap could be 100-250 people in earlier years. Amsterdam (DRW Europe B.V.), Tel Aviv, Dubai and Hong Kong counts are not found apart from HK ~20 in Nov 2025. Dutch KvK filings were not accessible.
4) The plan-year 2025 Form 5500 is not yet in the DOL dataset (Sep-2026 refresh), so there is no 2025 or 2026 US primary count.
5) The Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) was unreachable from this environment, so historical drw.com about/careers statements could not be checked. The FN London 2025 article and Bloomberg/Reuters originals were paywalled or blocked. The session's web-search budget (200 calls) ran out before 2019-2022 press, Crain's office-lease stories and London office-move coverage could be searched further; a follow-up session could continue.
6) Cumberland DRW's own headcount is unknown. ZoomInfo/LinkedIn show 51-200, and an undated FIA piece mentions ~10 people early on. Cumberland staff appear to be employed within DRW's US and UK payrolls.
7) No graduate-intake sizes were found.
evidence.red_flags:
1) Restatement: the DRW UK Partners LLP FY2023 accounts report 291 average staff for 2023, but the FY2024 accounts give 244 for 2023 (39 tech / 79 ops / 126 trading). Use 244, the later restated figure. 2023 wages also fell (£65.9m vs £84.6m in 2022) while reported headcount rose, so check for 2023 cost allocations or reclassification.
2) The DRW welfare benefit plan count is anomalous: 976 BOY to 1,725 EOY 2023, then 1,753 BOY to 1,205 EOY 2024. It tracked the 401(k) within ±5% in 2014-2022, so this looks like a definitional change. Do not use it as headcount.
3) US 401(k) counts are US-only and exclude ineligible staff such as some interns. Total participants (e.g. 1,625 EOY 2024) include former employees with balances; use the 'active' column. The 401(k) sponsor DRW Holdings LLC probably also covers non-trading affiliates (DRW Venture Capital, Convexity Properties, which are small).
4) LinkedIn-derived aggregators run systematically high. Revelio gives 2,067 (Q4 2023) vs ~1,700 press and ~1,750 bottom-up, and 2,468-2,543 (2025) vs 'over 2,000'. Revelio's YoY percentages don't match its own counts, and its regional subtotals don't add up. Tracxn's 2,500 is likely the same type of data.
5) Several stale or undated numbers circulate as current: Built In 1,825 (also older 1,600 and 1,145), MarketsWiki ~1,600 and >800, Bloomberg profile 460, The Ladders 1,000, LinkedIn 1,912. Some sites attach the global figure to single offices (Built In shows 1,825 for London, Montreal and Singapore pages).
6) 'Over 2,000' (drw.com, FIA bio, eFC job ads) is a self-promotional round floor that has been unchanged since at least early 2025.
7) The BFI bio says 'over 1,100 employees at its Chicago headquarters', and an aggregator snippet says 'over 1,200 at Chicago HQ'. These are Chicago-only figures and must not be read as firm-wide.
8) The UK LLP's turnover is cost-plus service income from group companies, not trading revenue. The '$176m adjusted loss' (FT via eFC) is a single desk's Q1 2026 loss, not firm-wide.
9) M&A step-changes: Chopper Trading (Jan 2015, ~180-200 staff, only part retained per 5500 data) and RGM Advisors (2017, ~70-80 staff) inflate 2015 and 2017 growth inorganically.
10) Period mismatch: UK figures are annual averages (fiscal years to March until 2019, December after), 401(k) figures are 31-Dec point-in-time counts, and press figures are point-in-time round numbers.
evidence.summary:
Headcount history for DRW (trading group including Cumberland), built from primary filings and checked against press. The best primary series is the US 401(k) active-participant count from the DOL Form 5500 datasets (sponsor DRW Holdings LLC, EIN 36-4331072), taken as year-end US headcount floors. The UK series is from Companies House accounts of DRW UK Partners LLP (annual averages, excluding members).

- **Canada:** 298 full-time plus 5 part-time (Mar 2026 profile).
- **Asia:** Singapore about 40 (2018), 60 (2023), about 70 (2024), 100 (Nov 2025), plus about 20 in Hong Kong.

The US 401(k) count runs at about 0.67-0.70 of the press firm-wide figures in 2016, 2018 and 2023, which supports using it as a scaling anchor.

draft.methodology: Only one firm-wide PnL figure exists: Bloomberg's FY2020 revenue of about $1.5bn (and EBITDA of about $750m), from people familiar during DRW's loan refinancing. The reported growth rates imply FY2019. Both years were converted to the project definition with a roughly 13% haircut for probable exchange and clearing fees and for VC and real-estate income (5-10% of net revenue per S&P). For 2015-2018 the hard anchor is the audited net trading revenue of DRW Investments, LLC (revenue minus commissions, execution and interest costs), DRW's main US prop-trading entity, which filed whole-entity accounts at Companies House until FY2018. It was scaled to the group using an assumed share of 40-70%, falling over time as Cumberland, Singapore, RGM and Houston energy were added. For 2021-2025, which have no figures, firm compensation was estimated as about 0.7x (0.55-0.9x) the UK LLP's audited all-in staff cost per head times average firm headcount. That factor reproduces the 2020 Bloomberg EBITDA margin. The resulting compensation was divided by an assumed comp ratio of 31-40%, and the direction was cross-checked against UK performance fees from affiliates, DRW Singapore results, rating-agency commentary and market regime. The 2026 row covers Q1 only, from an FT-reported adjusted loss of $176m whose scope (firm or power desk) is unresolved, so it is treated with scenario weighting. Headcount is built bottom-up from DOL Form 5500 US 401(k) active counts and UK LLP accounts, with estimates for other offices, and anchored to dated press and rating-agency figures.

Other units by now: DRW Singapore (S$83.7m total net revenue, about S$63m net of finance costs; profit before tax S$15.9m), Cumberland (the SEC complaint alleges more than $400m of revenue from Mar 2018 to Oct 2024, about $60m+ a year on average; an allegation in a case later dismissed), RGM, Houston, Canada and Europe. The DRWI share is assumed at 31-62% (mid 42%). The check is Bloomberg-implied 2019 group revenue of about $1.0bn against DRWI's 2018 total revenue of $376m, a share of about 35-40% in revenue terms. 2018 appears to have been a lean year for DRW's core. The low end is DRWI plus Singapore, Cumberland and other floors. Headcount: eFC, 8 Oct 2018, said DRW 'employs about 900 people globally'. US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 614 (welfare plan 633), a ratio of 0.68. UK average staff was 58 (FY to Mar-2019) and Singapore about 40.

PnL is derived from Bloomberg (18 Jun 2021; people familiar; figures circulating during DRW's term-loan process): 2020 revenue rose 50% to about $1.5bn and EBITDA rose 67% to about $750m. That implies 2019 revenue of about $1.0bn (about $0.94-1.07bn given the rounding of 'about' and '50%') and 2019 EBITDA of about $450m. 2019 was not reported directly. The same ~13-14% haircut as 2020 converts this to the project definition: about 8-10% for exchange, clearing and brokerage fees if Bloomberg's 'revenue' is before them (DRWI's trading expenses were 13-22% of revenue in 2014-18), and about 5-10% for VC and real estate (S&P), giving about $860m. net_income_usd_m is a proxy: implied EBITDA of about $450m less small term-loan interest (the first $300m loan came only in Nov 2019), depreciation and amortisation, and foreign taxes. It is a holding-level figure that includes VC and real estate; actual net income was not reported. DRW Singapore company-only revenue was flat (S$83.7m). Headcount: Moody's (Nov 2019 release on the $300m term loan) said 'the firm has grown steadily to over 1000 employees operating in ten offices'. US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 688 (welfare plan 676) and UK average staff was 65 (Apr-Dec 2019). Bottom-up gives about 1,000-1,030.

The only firm-wide annual PnL figure found. Bloomberg (18 Jun 2021): 'At futures, options and cryptocurrencies trader DRW Holdings LLC, revenue and Ebitda surged in 2020 by 50% and 67%, respectively, to about $1.5 billion and $750 million, people familiar with the matter said.' This was verified only through several matching snippets of syndicated copies; the Bloomberg page could not be fetched. S&P (Feb 2021) said 'profitability was up considerably in 2020' and Moody's cited strong 2020 earnings. 'Revenue' is undefined and is at DRW Holdings level. The mid of $1.30bn is $1.5bn x ~0.92 (probable exchange and clearing fees, if revenue was stated before them) x ~0.94 (VC and real estate removed). The high of $1.56bn allows that revenue was already net of fees and VC was small. The low of $1.05bn allows revenue gross of fees, a larger VC/crypto-equity share in 2020 and rounding of 'about'. Corroboration: DRW Singapore company-only revenue more than doubled to S$195m (profit before tax S$84m), and UK LLP all-in staff cost was £423k ($543k) per head. A 50% EBITDA margin implies firm comp of about $400-450m, roughly 0.7x the UK cost per head times about 1,060 average staff. That calibrates the comp-scaling used for 2021-2025. net_income_usd_m is a proxy: EBITDA of about $750m less interest on the ~$300m term loan, depreciation and amortisation, and foreign taxes. It is holding-level, includes VC and real estate, and is not reported. Headcount is derived: US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 746 (+8%; welfare plan 718) and UK average staff was 63. Bottom-up: US 746 + UK ~70 + Canada ~170 (estimated) + Singapore ~45 + other ~35, about 1,080.

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists. Qualitative evidence: Moody's upgraded DRW to Ba2 in Oct 2021, citing 'strong performance thus far in 2021'. The $500m term loan was refinanced in Feb 2021. Signals are mixed. It was a crypto boom year (Cumberland; any DRW VC gains are excluded from scope). DRW Singapore company-only revenue fell 42% to S$112.5m (profit before tax S$24.8m vs S$84m), while UK LLP all-in staff cost per head was flat ($549k vs $543k). Comp-scaling: $549k x 0.7 x ~1,155 average staff gives about $445m of firm comp, which at a 31-35% comp ratio implies $1.27-1.43bn. The mid is $1.35bn, about flat on 2020. Bars run -30%/+40% because the UK-to-firm pay factor (0.55-0.9) and the comp ratio are both assumptions. Headcount is derived: US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 826 (+11%; welfare plan 800) and UK average staff was 94. Bottom-up: US 826 + UK ~120 + Canada ~190 (estimated) + Singapore ~50 + other ~40, about 1,230.

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists. The available signals point to a peak year. UK LLP wages rose to £84.6m for 169 staff, about £500k per head in wages and £570k ($705k) all-in, against £347k of wages per head in 2021, which marks a big bonus year. UK performance fees from affiliates were £122.7m (restated), the highest per UK trader in the series. DRW Singapore profit before tax was S$70.4m, against S$24.8m in 2021. The regime was record rates and energy/commodity volatility, which is DRW's core (S&P says DRW is more weighted to rates than its peers). The FTX/crypto crash in 2022 is a possible drag through Cumberland. Comp-scaling: $705k x 0.7 x ~1,340 average staff gives about $660m of firm comp, which at a 31-36% comp ratio implies $1.83-2.13bn. The mid is trimmed to $1.85bn because UK desks probably outperformed the US in the 2022 European energy crisis, so the 0.7 factor may overstate firm pay. Headcount is derived: US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 967 (+17%; welfare plan 938; the filing is an amended Oct 2024 submission) and UK average staff was 169 (+80%). Bottom-up: US 967 + UK ~200 + Canada ~220 (estimated) + Singapore ~55 + other ~50, about 1,490.

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists. Moody's (Nov 2023, relayed by the primary lens) cited 'solid financial performance in 2023 to date'. Signals point to a step down from 2022. UK LLP wages fell to £65.9m even though staff rose; all-in cost was £312k ($388k) per head on the restated 244 average staff. UK performance fees fell 30% to £86.5m. DRW Singapore profit before tax fell to S$47.7m, and its revenue was restated to S$121m. The FT's 'Singapore subsidiary brought in $312mn in net revenues last year' reflects the original accounts, which grossed up about S$292m of repo interest offset by about S$292m of finance costs and were later restated. That figure is not used. Comp-scaling: $388k x 0.7 x ~1,620 average staff gives about $440m of firm comp, which at a 31-35% comp ratio implies $1.26-1.42bn; the mid is $1.35bn. Headcount: The TRADE (3 Jul 2023) said 'roughly 1700 members of staff globally', with about 60 in Singapore. US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 1,174 (+21%). The welfare plan's 1,725 is anomalous and not used. UK average staff was 244 as restated in the FY2024 accounts (291 originally). Bottom-up at year-end: US 1,174 + UK ~290 + Canada ~250 (estimated) + Singapore/HK ~70 + other ~60, about 1,820-1,850. Revelio's Q4 2023 figure of 2,067 is LinkedIn-modelled and biased high.

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists (the FT, Nov 2024: 'Its revenue and profit figures are private'). S&P (Feb 2025) described 'good, albeit lower-than-peer profitability' and said 2024 results were 'good, but not as strong' as competitors', because DRW is less exposed to equity volatility and more to rates. Moody's cited 'solid financial performance in 2024 to date'. The term loan was refinanced at $900m (Jun 2024) and upsized by $250m in Dec 2024 to $1.15bn to add trading capital, which shows lender confidence in earnings. S&P puts VC and real estate at 5-10% of net revenue, which is excluded here. UK performance fees rose 56% to £135.2m, and UK all-in cost was £371k ($474k) per head. DRW Singapore's profit before tax of S$91m was mostly a S$93m dividend from a subsidiary, implying a strong European/Dutch subsidiary. Comp-scaling: $474k x 0.7 x ~1,930 average staff gives about $640m of firm comp, which at a 33-38% comp ratio (higher because of the lower-than-peer profitability) implies $1.68-1.94bn; the mid is $1.8bn. The recent lens's judgment of about $2.4bn sits within the bars but is not adopted as the mid, given S&P's explicit statement that DRW lagged its peers. Cumberland was described by Moody's as 'relatively small'. Headcount: the FT (Nov 2024) said 'about 2,100 staff'. US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 1,262, about 60% of 2,100, and UK average staff was 322. Bottom-up: US 1,262 + UK ~350 + Canada ~285 + Asia ~90 + other ~70, about 2,060.

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists. Signals are mixed. UK performance fees from affiliates rose 15% to £155.9m, UK wages per head rose 6% to £340.9k and UK staff costs rose 26% to £150.4m. The UK LLP swung to a £3.4m loss, but it is a cost-plus service entity whose result is a transfer-pricing residual, not trading PnL, and the UK trading companies' results are swept by transfer pricing (DRW Investments (UK) Ltd revenue was £0.3m after a £20.5m adjustment). DRW Singapore's own trading gains fell 56% to S$46.2m and its profit before tax fell to S$21.1m from S$91.3m. DRW reports record ETF volume of $1.9T in 2025 (volume, not PnL), and 2025 saw record industry volumes (the April tariff shock). Comp-scaling: $528k x 0.7 x ~2,140 average staff gives about $790m of firm comp, which at a 35-40% comp ratio implies $1.98-2.26bn. The mid is trimmed to $1.95bn for the Singapore weakness and because UK pay growth outran UK performance fees. Bars are wide and skewed upward to allow for a strong industry year. Headcount is derived: UK average staff was 376 (+54). eFC (Nov 2025, unnamed sources) put Singapore at about 100 and Hong Kong at about 20. DRW Canada reported 298 full-time staff (Mar 2026 profile, probably 2025 data). The US is about 1,340 (estimated; the plan-year 2025 Form 5500 is not yet in the DOL data). The FIA (Mar 2025) and Wikipedia citing Financial News both say 'over 2,000'/2,000. Revelio's Q4 2025 figure of 2,468 is LinkedIn-modelled and biased high by about 15-20%.

rows.notes: Q1 2026 only, the latest period with any PnL data. eFinancialCareers (4 Aug 2026), citing the FT (12 Jun 2026; FT text not accessed), says DRW parted ways with its North American head of power and gas trading 'after the firm made an adjusted loss of $176m in the first quarter of 2026'. The FT headline, as quoted, says the 'Group took $176mn hit' on power markets during winter volatility. Moody's placed DRW's Ba2 rating on review for downgrade on 16 Jun 2026, citing a trading-risk appetite 'higher than peers' and earnings volatility; the outcome is unknown. Both the scope (firm or desk) and the definition of 'adjusted' are unresolved, so three scenarios are weighed. (a) A firm-wide adjusted loss after costs: adding back about $200-260m of Q1 fixed costs (salaries, technology, occupancy, minimal bonus accrual) gives net trading revenue of about +$20m to +$90m. (b) A firm-wide trading-level loss gives about -$176m. (c) A loss on the power/gas desk only, with the rest of the firm at a run-rate of about $450-500m a quarter, gives about +$250m to +$350m. The mid of +$50m is roughly the median; the probability-weighted mean is about +$100m. The 90% interval is -$220m to +$420m. This is not an annual figure, and nothing after 31 Mar 2026 was found. Headcount: drw.com (fetched Oct 2026, undated copy) says 'over 2,000 employees'. Revelio (Mar 2026, 2,528) and Tracxn (Sep 2026, 2,500) are LinkedIn-modelled and biased high by about 15-20%. Built In shows 1,825, undated and probably stale. UK staff grew by 54 in 2025, and hiring may have slowed after the Q1 loss. Mid is 2,250.

ytd_2026.description: Q1 2026 only. The only 2026 PnL data point is the FT-reported (12 Jun 2026, via eFinancialCareers 4 Aug 2026) 'adjusted loss of $176m in the first quarter of 2026', linked to North American power and gas trading during winter-storm volatility. It is unclear whether the figure is firm-wide or desk-level, and whether it is before or after compensation. The project-definition estimate of Q1 net trading revenue (before compensation) is a mid of +$50m with a 90% interval of -$220m to +$420m, scenario-weighted. No H1, Q3 or YTD figure after 31 Mar 2026 was found. Moody's put DRW on review for downgrade on 16 Jun 2026, outcome unknown. Headcount is the latest estimate, about 2,250 (mid/late 2026).

The draft's factual base mostly checks out against the sources I could open. The changes I propose are small. Main limit: this turn's web-search budget was already used up, so I could not run independent searches for firm-wide revenue figures the draft may have missed. I worked by fetching the cited sources directly and OCR'ing the primary filings. The Bloomberg article of Jun 2021 (HTTP 403) and the FT article of Jun 2026 (blocked) could not be opened, so the $1.5bn/$750m FY2020 anchor and the scope of the Q1 2026 $176m loss remain unverified.

Verified exactly:
- Headcount anchors: Reuters 725 (Dec 2016); Bloomberg via Traders Magazine 'more than 500' (Jan 2015) and '700-person' (Mar 2016); eFC 'about 900' and Singapore 40 (Oct 2018); Moody's 'over 1000 employees operating in ten offices' (Nov 2019); The TRADE 'roughly 1700' and Singapore 60 (Jul 2023); FT 'about 2,100 staff' and 'revenue and profit figures are private' (Nov 2024); FIA and drw.com 'over 2,000' (plus 800+ technologists on drw.com); eFC Singapore 100 and Hong Kong 20 (Nov 2025).
- DOL Form 5500 counts from the raw DOL datasets: 401(k) active participants of 746 (2020), 967 (2022), 1,174 (2023) and 1,262 (2024); welfare plan 718, 938, 1,725 and 1,205. The plan-year 2025 DRW 401(k) filing is not yet in the DOL dataset as of its 30 Sep 2026 update.
- DRW Investments, LLC FY2015-2018 accounts: every revenue, trading-expense and net-income figure.
- UK LLP 2022-2025 accounts: average staff 169 / 291 (restated to 244) / 322 / 376; staff costs £96.3m / £76.0m / £119.4m / £150.4m.
- DRW Singapore figures, with SGD confirmed as the functional currency. The FT's '$312mn' is S$408.8m converted to USD.
- SEC complaint: Cumberland generated more than $400m of revenue and more than $27m of profit, Mar 2018 to present (Oct 2024).
- Rating-agency texts: S&P Feb 2025 (5-10% of net revenue from VC and real estate; 'good, albeit lower-than-peer profitability'); Moody's Dec 2024; Moody's Jun 2026, which contains no figures.

Problems found:
- The 2020 anchor is labelled reported_press but is really derived. DRW's own gross-revenue presentation suggests a slightly larger trading-cost haircut, so the 2019 and 2020 mids should come down by about 5%.
- The UK performance-fee series omits fees received from members (2022 total £153.3m, not '£122.7m restated'; 2023 total £102.7m). The quoted year-on-year changes are therefore wrong, but the levels the draft settles on remain consistent with the corrected series.
- The 2025 'Singapore weakness' trim misreads a booking change: service fees nearly doubled and there are S$1.65bn of related-party trading gains.
- The Q1 2026 FT headline quote cannot be traced, and the eFC wording favours a firm-level loss, which argues for trimming the upside.
- The 2019 headcount low bound sits below Moody's '>1000' floor.
- Smaller source mis-attributions, listed in the last challenge.

The 2015-2018 rows (scaled from DRWI with an assumed share) and the 2021-2025 rows (scaled from UK comp) are still assumption-driven. The UK staff mix changed a lot (technology staff went from 39 to 111 in 2023-25), which makes the UK-to-firm comp factor unstable, but the bars are wide enough. I found no authoritative figure that contradicts any row. The DRW Holdings consolidated accounts exist (per the UK LLP notes) but are not public. Moody's and S&P full reports, and lender materials, are still the best path to real 2021-2025 figures.

challenges.issue: For 2021-2025, PnL per head is produced by the model's own formula, not observed. Each mid is 0.7 x UK LLP all-in staff cost per head x modelled average headcount / an assumed comp ratio, so PnL per head is just the UK pay-per-head series rescaled. On top of that, the comp-ratio bands drift above the ~31% that the 2020 calibration actually implies. This pulls the mids down by 5-24%, most of all in 2025.
challenges.evidence:
Recomputed from the draft's own inputs. Firm comp = 0.7 x UK cost/head x average heads: 2021 0.7 x $549k x 1,155 = $444m; 2022 0.7 x $705k x 1,340 = $661m; 2023 0.7 x $388k x 1,620 = $440m; 2024 0.7 x $474k x 1,930 = $640m; 2025 0.7 x $528k x 2,140 = $791m. Draft PnL mid per average head is $1.17m, $1.38m, $0.83m, $0.93m and $0.91m. That is 2.13x, 1.96x, 2.14x, 1.96x and 1.73x the UK cost/head, which is simply 0.7 / comp ratio, less the judgment trims.

The 2020 calibration is 0.7 x $543k x 1,060 = $403m of comp against the $1,300m PnL mid. That is a 31.0% comp ratio, or a 2.26x multiplier. The later comp-ratio bands centre on 33% (2021, 2023), 33.5% (2022), 35.5% (2024) and 37.5% (2025). With the calibrated pair (0.7, 31%) the mids would be $1.44bn, $2.13bn, $1.42bn, $2.06bn and $2.55bn. The draft mids are 94%, 87%, 95%, 87% and 76% of those values.

A rising comp ratio in weaker years can be argued, but it is the main driver of the 2024-2025 mids, and its only DRW-specific support is S&P's 'lower-than-peer profitability'. That describes a level, which the 2020 calibration already captures.

Because PnL is proportional to modelled average headcount, PnL and headcount errors are positively correlated by construction. build.py's per-head band assumes independent errors, so for 2021-2025 the per-head band should reflect only the factor and comp-ratio uncertainty. The per-head series should be labelled as model-derived: UK pay per head divided by the comp ratio.
